text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Attorney General in opinion to President Weizman: no justification for general amnesty on state's 50th anniversary.
- United States to strengthen guarantees of interim accords; to suggest compromise dates for end of West Bank redeployments.
- Egypt asks to post army forces in place of police units on Israel border.
- Secret service budget 2.45 billion shekels this year.
- Defence Minister Mordechai: security services must restrain extremists in Hebron.
- Deputy Housing Minister Porush to approve building of 200 houses in Katzrin on Golan in addition to 96 approved units.
- Three additional tax steps to close 270 million shekel gap in budget.
JERUSALEM POST
- United States to make compromise pullback bid.
- Mordechai: Syria keeps open diplomatic, military options.
- Syria: bombing aimed at changing our Israel policy.
- Swiss may repay Jewish groups in 'goodwill gesture'.
- Body of Egyptian infiltrator found.
- Budget deficit at 14.4 billion shekels, nearly double projection.
- Japanese firm mulls $300 million Negev cement plant.
- Swiss bank shares weakened by Jewish boycott fears.
- Egyptian tycoon to buy Koor shares.
MAARIV
- Prime Minister Netanyahu raises new proposal to delay completion of redeployments in territories until 1999. U.S. envoy Ross attempts new compromise proposals to allow deal.
- Settlers: we'll bulldoze Palestinian 'settlements'.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Shin Bet secret service increases security on Mordechai.
- Senior U.S. official: Hebron deal at hand.
